answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 717 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the summit audit recomputes usage from the zenith history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. A farm running 113 keys thus pays for 113 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the ripple declaration. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
